slot.brief: Find the domain of a function involving a square root and a denominator (e.g., √(polynomial)/(rational expression)); intersect the positivity condition with the denominator-nonzero condition.

verdicts.working: Require x²−4≥0, so x≤−2 or x≥2; also exclude x=3. This gives option A.

working:
$x^2-4\geq 0\Rightarrow x\leq-2\text{ or }x\geq2$.
$x-3\neq0\Rightarrow x\neq3$.
$\text{Domain}=(-\infty,-2]\cup[2,3)\cup(3,\infty)$

Independent check: Require x²−4≥0, so x≤−2 or x≥2; also exclude x=3. This gives option A.
solution:
The square root requires $x^2-4\geq 0$, so $x\leq -2$ or $x\geq 2$. The denominator requires $x\neq 3$.
Thus the domain is $(-\infty,-2]\cup[2,3)\cup(3,\infty)$.
